page: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is an ARM-based general-purpose server powered by 96 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz. Hyper-V allocates one thread per physical core without simultaneous multithreading, eliminating resource contention between logical threads. The CPU subsystem is supported by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 384.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a balanced 4.0 GB per core allocation. Local storage consists of a 5669 GB NVMe solid-state drive, providing substantial high-speed scratch space directly on the host node, while no GPU accelerators are included.

Performance testing reveals strong scaling in parallel execution environments. Benchmark results place multi-core stress testing, Clang software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression within top-tier percentiles. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth achieves 464.68 GB/sec for reads and 205.46 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-core benchmarks, such as single-threaded stress testing and Geekbench single-core tests, settle into median brackets. The trade-off centers on aggregate core parallelism rather than maximum per-core clock frequency, making overall throughput dependent on application concurrency.

Resource density offers favorable operational efficiency for distributed enterprise services. The combination of high physical core density, high memory bandwidth, and 5669 GB of local NVMe storage matches the requirements of large-scale caching systems, database engines, and continuous integration pipelines. Top-tier metrics in Redis operations, static web serving, and database benchmarks validate its capability for I/O-intensive services. Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 serves as a balanced platform for web serving clusters, large compilation farms, containerized microservices, and high-throughput data processing workflows requiring consistent parallel compute.
description: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture, powered by 96 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 physical cores operating at 3.4 GHz with no simultaneous multithreading. It features 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core, alongside 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server includes no discrete GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute capability, software compilation throughput, and memory bandwidth, reaching 464.68 GB/sec in large-block reads and 205.46 GB/sec in large-block writes. Single-core performance falls within average ranges, reflecting the architecture focus on core density over peak single-thread execution. High throughput in Redis transactions and database operations highlights its balanced architecture. Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is tailored for scalable web tier deployments, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation, in-memory caching, and data processing environments benefiting from high physical core counts and fast local NVMe storage.
